subject.title: fix(browser): keep CDP cursor text previews UTF-16 safe

question: Should browser cursor previews guarantee that no truncation-created lone surrogate crosses the CDP `returnByValue` boundary even though the existing Node stage already guarantees safe final preview text, and should this PR own that invariant?
rationale: The patch is technically supported and behavior-preserving, but the value of an additional intermediate-wire invariant and selection of the canonical competing branch are ownership decisions rather than mechanical correctness repairs.

options.title: Adopt this hardening
options.body: Keep this PR as the canonical implementation because it provides live CDP proof, preserves final behavior, and covers trailing-high-surrogate residue as well as split pairs.

options.title: Use the competing branch
options.body: Close this PR only after confirming that the actual browser changes in the competing PR provide equivalent page-scope safety, proof, and regression coverage.

options.title: Keep current behavior
options.body: Decline transport-only hardening because the existing two-stage pipeline already guarantees safe final cursor preview text.

recommendation.title: Adopt this hardening
recommendation.body: Keep this PR as the canonical implementation because it provides live CDP proof, preserves final behavior, and covers trailing-high-surrogate residue as well as split pairs.
